newsitem.title: LATVIA: Ruhrgas, Preussen say Latvia investment long-term.
newsitem.headline: Ruhrgas, Preussen say Latvia investment long-term.

text.p: German gas firms Ruhrgas and Preussen said on Wednesday that the purchase of a 16.25 percent stake in Latvian Gas was a long-term investment.
The two German firms formed a consortium to buy the Latvian Gas stake while Russian Gazprom bought 16.25 percent on its own.

"We do not want to make 'quick money' but in the long-term view to make a profit from the development potential of the Latvian energy market," Ruhrgas vice-chairman Burckhard Bergmann told a news conference.
"Our aim is to give a solid basis so that Latvian Gas can become a successful business," he added.
The German consortium paid 14.6 million lats for their stake in Latvian Gas but under the sale agreement some 55 million lats of investments will be put into the gas company this year.
It is the first of the Latvian utilities to be sold by the government and a stake in electricity company Latvenergo is also up for privatisation.
The sale agreement with the German firms was supposed to be signed earlier this year but was delayed due to the Western firms' worries over the debts of Latvian Gas.
But the government agreed to to cut the debts by around 30 million lats.

"The economic space around the sea in our opinion will develop as one of the most important regions in Europe and the development of the energy system will have enormous importance," Preussen board member Andreas Eichholtz said.
He also said that the creation of an energy system in Latvia that would meet international standards would also be possible in the medium term as the sale of Latvenergo gets underway.
